worst_places.after:
One line of code crosses all three layers. When you write `await fs.promises.readFile(...)`:

1. V8 runs your async code and manages the Promise.
2. The Node API wraps the call into a form libuv understands.
3. libuv decides how to actually perform it — on the thread pool, or through an async API of the operating system (OS).

The layers are covered in detail in [The Event Loop] and [libuv and the Thread Pool]; the Promise part is in [Microtasks, Macrotasks, and process.nextTick].

patterns: ALL-CAPS is the zone's default emphasis marker, and it is used to the point of self-defeat: 20-63 shouted words per file (ru/09: 54, ru/10: 57, en/09: 63), often 2-3 per paragraph — «между КАЖДОЙ парой фаз», «дренируется ПОЛНОСТЬЮ», "between EVERY pair of phases", "the SET OF AVAILABLE APIs". When everything is capitalised nothing is emphasised, and on a phone the paragraph reads as a rant. It also has a concrete side effect: the mechanical abbreviation checker reports ~100 false positives (EVERY, EACH, ONE, THE, AT, WHAT, ВСЮ, ЗАХОД, КАЖДОЕ), which buries the ~60 real unexpanded acronyms it also found. Bold already exists in these files and is used correctly elsewhere — the fix is to convert emphasis to bold and keep caps only for literal identifiers.

Every acronym is treated as shared vocabulary. Across all 20 files, not one of GC, CPU, OS/ОС, DNS, TCP, IOCP, JIT, IC, RSS, OOM, TTL, DTO, ORM, TDZ, APM, k8s, cgroup, БД, p99 is expanded at its first use in the file it appears in — GC is used 7x in article 08 and 10x in article 10 without ever being written out once. Only AST and NDJSON get the treatment the whole zone needs (`AST (Abstract Syntax Tree)`), which shows the authors know the pattern and simply did not apply it. Because articles are read out of order and the site has ten of them, 'GC' has to be spelled out ten times.

The structural habit is strong and worth protecting: almost every section opens with a diagram, a table, or a ❌/✅ code pair, and only then explains. The damage is concentrated in the *closing* paragraph of each such section — a single 40-80-word sentence, hung together with two or three em-dashes, that tries to state the mechanism, the practical consequence, the interview framing, and a cross-reference at once (en/02 81w, ru/02 68w, en/01 56w, ru/08 56w, en/06 57w). These paragraphs are the highest-value target in the zone: splitting each into 3-4 sentences would fix B and F without touching a single technical claim, a diagram, or a code example.

Articles 04, 09 and 10 open by defining the *shallow* answer before giving the real one — «Поверхностный уровень этой темы — "выучить порядок..."», "The shallow level is 'CommonJS uses require...'" — so the first thing on screen is knowledge the reader is being told not to rely on, and the actual answer arrives 40-60 words later. Articles 01, 05, 07 do the opposite and are the strongest in the zone (07 opens with the failing `readFile` snippet, and its scores are the highest). Where the meta-framing is worth keeping, it belongs after the answer, not in front of it.
notes:
Cross-references (`[The Event Loop]`) are plain bracketed text — there are zero markdown links in all 20 files. This hurts: article 01 spends two 45-56-word sentences listing titles the reader cannot follow, and there is no consistent naming — `[Memory and GC]` (ru/05) vs `[Memory and Garbage Collection]`, `[CommonJS vs ESM]` (01) vs `[CommonJS vs ES Modules]` (10). Article 06 also points to `[WebSockets and Realtime Systems]` and `[Scalability and Load Balancing]`, which are outside this topic.
Factual/consistency slips a reader will notice: both locales of article 10 say "каждый из 45 вопросов выше" / "each of the 45 questions above" but only 33 numbered questions exist; en/06 comments `// modern API, see below` on `os.availableParallelism()` and nothing below discusses it; ru/03 has a Latin 'a' inside «оперaций»; ru/09 has «серверless-функций» mixing scripts; ru/02 has «монографичности» for «мономорфности».
The `<!-- verified: 2026-06-05 -->` marker is present in all 10 ru files and in none of the en files.
RU-specific vocabulary to standardise: «дренируется/дренаж» → «опустошается»; «вулнерабилити» → «уязвимости»; «orchestrator» → «оркестратор» (08 already does this); the apostrophe transliterations «callback'а / chunk'и / instance'ами / trade-off'ами / follow-up'ы / tree-shake'ит» appear in most files and are the single loudest signal of translated-from-English prose.
Nothing in this zone needs its depth cut: the technical content (megamorphic call sites, dual package hazard, external vs heapUsed, dns.lookup pool contention) is the reason the site is worth reading and every worst_place rewrite above preserves it verbatim.
